title: Inspectors' code: Steenackers to Mercadier, Tours to Paris, 2 November 1870 (Pillon collection, Depeches officielles 2me serie no. 1)

documents.shelfmark: Alexandre Pillon collection (private), pigeon dispatch 'Depeches officielles, 2me serie n 1' (file 2emeS-1)

plaintext.source: No plaintext of this telegram is known. It is not in Steenackers 1883 (searched on HathiTrust), the Enquete parlementaire, Favre, Dagron or the 1872 Societe d'acclimatation article. The Algeria volume of the Enquete prints December 1870 telegrams headed 'Chiffre des inspecteurs' in plaintext only, without ciphertext.

transcription.source: Alexandre Pillon (collector), transcription of his scan; digit strings of the key runs rechecked against the scan by the project
transcription.notes: 736 four-digit coded groups (343 distinct) mixed with 437 clear words (names, addresses, ordinary words), counts from NOTES and the wiki. The transcription file is now in the repository (inspecteurs_2nov_partial.txt, published with the collector's permission of 8 Nov 2026); a plain regex for four-digit strings finds 754 (349 distinct) in it, which includes four-digit numbers in clear text, so the 736/343 coded-group count has not been reconciled with the file and 'measured' stays false. The clear words are in the original (Pillon). Snips of his scan are on the site.

system.summary: A four-digit code whose table is an alphabetical lexicon laid out over 0000-9999 (words and syllables), with beacon groups (0101, 0201, 0301, 0102 ...) that bracket words spelled in syllable groups; mixed with clear words in one telegram.
system.notes: Alphabetical order was inferred by the project from 13 syllable values and 7 whole words that fit their alphabetical positions to about 0.012-0.016 (a random mapping about 0.33); Pillon had suggested the code was almost alphabetical. The meaning of the beacons is open. The prefects' code R1 in Pillon's collection is a different table (18% overlap against 10% by chance). The Favre / delegation code (Chaudordy letter of 18 Dec 1870) is a different cipher and is not part of this profile.

prior_solution.where: No reading of this telegram is known. Pillon's own readings (5926 = recu, 0603 = depeche, 2215 = capitale) were suggestions and fail the alphabetical test.

conditions.human_role: Alexandre Pillon owns and transcribed the material, sent the scan, and answered the project's questions by email (the clear words are original, the beacon idea, the alphabetical hint, readings that were then tested and some withdrawn). Daniel Bourdeau forwarded the collection link, sent short drafts to Pillon and decided what to share. No other target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Received Pillon's collection (a 2.9 GB share); fetched the spreadsheets and documents, later the scans. The inspectors' telegram is one item in it: a mixed clear and coded pigeon dispatch headed 'Tours 2 Novembre (chiffre des inspecteurs)'.
Counted the telegram: 1,173 tokens = 736 four-digit groups (343 distinct) + 437 clear words; commonest groups 0101 (49), 0201 (31), 0301 (28), 4914, 2119, 8328.
Word-bigram fill-in, one word per group (inspecteurs_cloze.py): log-probability -7085 for random fills, -5025 for the fit, but the output is dominated by 'de' and 'la'.

Looked for a printed text of the telegram: Steenackers 1883 (Gallica needed a human check; HathiTrust in-book search), the Enquete parlementaire, Favre, Dagron, the 1872 Societe d'acclimatation article. No passage matched.
Compared the telegram's groups with the prefects' code R1: 18% occur in R1's table (10% by chance) and the values make no sense in context.

Name crib on the repeated runs between beacons, using the clear heading: 8328 9214 0218 4906 3316 8328 = S-TEEN-A-K-ER-S, 5504 1122 2514 3316 = MER-CA-DI-ER, 6816 4001 6129 8328 = PI-GE-ON-S; 8328 = S, 3316 = ER and 6129 = ON each recur in two words. The first guess (ER-NEST-MER-CA-DI-ER) was not supported.

Alphabetical test: placed the 13 syllable values in an alphabetical French word list; the fractional position predicts value/9999 with mean error 0.012-0.016 (random mapping about 0.33). Pillon's readings 5926 = recu, 0603 = depeche and 2215 = capitale each sit about 0.18 off and fail the rule.
Checked the key digit strings of the telegram against Pillon's scan (enlarged crops): the transcribed runs match digit for digit.

Spelled-run solver (spell_solver.py): splits candidate strings so each piece fits its alphabetical position. Known strings rank in the top 0.5% of 24,000-31,000 candidates (pigeons 8, Mercadier 30, ballon 145, Steenackers 6-8): it shortlists, it does not decode.

Chance test for 9113 8317 1504 = T-RO-CHU: one string of 28,897 fits as closely; about 0.15% chance that some of 51 names fits that closely by luck. The Nantes name 9802 6124 = Vinoy fits but 0.7% of strings fit as closely: dropped.

Blind genre check: predicted before computing that the last paragraph passes family news ('est bien portante', 'en bonne sante'). 3407 = est, 7027 0312 = PORT-ANTE, 1026 8416 = bonne sante and 4007 = general fit within 0.000-0.011 of their positions; a random word pair fits two random groups within 0.01 each in 0.05% of trials.

Tested Pillon's decomposition MER = 5511 + 6819 3412 = CAD-IER against the alphabetical rule: mean error 0.23 against 0.010 for MER-CA-DI-ER. Pillon then withdrew it (a different recipient stands before Mercadier).

Benchmark loop on 10 items with independent support (bench_loop.py, rule: one hypothesis per loop, stop after 3 rejections). Position only MRR 0.190; with a frequency prior 0.565; with a bigram context 0.615. R1-based calibration, a short-piece prior and a name bonus were rejected.

Joint beam-Viterbi decoder over the whole telegram (joint_loop.py): 3 of 20 gold word occurrences with whole-word groups only, 11 of 20 when beacon-bracketed runs may be one spelled word. Free segmentation, consistency voting and neighbour bounds added nothing. Misses: bonne|sante, portante, ballon.

Acceptance engine rebuilt on a wiki (wiki/tools/engine.py), calibrated by blinding the supported entries. Three runs accepted readings that review found unsupported (six frequent words and 'insurrection'; 'le' spelled l|e; 'picard' plus overwritten entries) and were rolled back, each producing a rule. The final gate proposed 355 units and accepted none.

Piece-level consistency across spelled runs (leave-one-unit-out): pigeons, Mercadier and Steenackers are recovered but fail their null tests; ballon = bal|l|on is not confirmed by fixed pieces (bataillon fits as well by position).

Topic prior from pigeon-post text (Dagron 1871 and the 1872 article, 23,433 words): benchmark MRR 0.615 -> 0.707, and 'ballon' moves from rank 13 to rank 1. Words absent from the topic corpus (sante, portante) drop slightly.

Looked for a second text in the same code in Pillon's collection: best overlap of any other piece with the telegram's 343 distinct groups is 6.2% against 3.4% by chance. No cross-validation text exists in the collection.
Searched for the Nantes and Rennes correspondents named in the last paragraph (Dagron, Steenackers 1883 on HathiTrust, the 1872 article, archive.org full text): none identified.

Pilot of reading page scans with Claude, on one telegram the collector had already typed by hand: 271 of 283 groups exactly right (95.8%); every miss was one digit (3/8, 1/2, 9/0), 8 of the 12 flagged by the reader.

At the collector's request, transcribed 12 untranscribed page scans (about 14,000 groups) by reading them with Claude. The transcriptions were made for the collector and are shared with him only; they are not in this repository.

Independent re-reads of the weak pages. Four spots cannot be read from these scans (one Favre block on the 23 Oct page, the top 14 lines of one page, the lower part of one small block, one blurry block) and one page is unreadable. A group-level quality note went to the collector with the workbook.

Codebook decode against the collector's R1 repertoire: the 24 Oct Gambetta-to-Favre telegram reads with R1 (word-pair test z=18.8 against shuffled order, coverage 94%); the Steenackers-to-Trochu blocks of the 23 Oct page are R1 by coverage (80-90%) and by group-frequency profile (cosine 0.83-0.90).

Codebook decode against the collector's R2 ('chiffre nouveau') repertoire: the 13 Nov Tours telegram decodes with R2 (z=4.1, coverage 89%) and is Gambetta to Favre of 13 Nov, printed in the Enquete parlementaire, Depeches telegraphiques officielles, tome II pp. 302-304 (first third also in Favre vol. 2 pp. 108-110). The decode matches the printed sentence on Thiers's double failure and the passages on the Russian pretensions, England and a general congress.

Family classification of the new blocks by group-frequency profile and codebook coverage. Favre-addressed telegrams of 8, 10, 19 Nov and 5 Dec and the 23 Oct Favre block belong to the Favre/delegation code (cosine 0.53-0.75 to the pooled family; 701119 is 0.62); one block (7 Dec table, third) is unplaced. Cosine alone does not separate R2 from the Favre code (the R2 page scores 0.45 against the Favre family), so the codebook decode is the test. R2 and the Favre code are both frequency-ordered numberings with homophones (rank correlation of number with frequency -0.40 and -0.43); a rank-for-rank decode scores about zero.

Favre code topic run on the doubled pool (17,658 positions; 7,504 new usable groups; within-letter shuffle null, Bonferroni). Replicating on the new half alone: 628 with 1792 (la before conference) 3/15, p=0.027; 620 with 1915, 5/8, p=0.001; 1908 with 1915, 4/9, p=0.017. 1440 does not replicate; 310 with 1915 (13/51) passes and survives correction; 151/888 borderline and not claimed; 146 and 121 untestable. Date profile null (45 groups at p<0.05 against a 95th percentile of 52 under shuffled dates). No word values from topic clusters.
Codebook size of the Favre code: Chao1 lower bound about 2,200 (three per cent of tokens are groups seen once). Corrects the earlier statement that it was larger than 2,300, which it was not.

Searched printed texts for the other new telegrams: no match except 13 Nov. The 7 Dec table is probably Chaudordy's dispatch of 7 Dec (Favre vol. 2 p. 255 says it reached Paris 15 Dec); the full text is probably in the Quai d'Orsay papers (not checked).

Aligned the 13 Nov R2 decode with the printed text to fill gaps in the collector's R2 repertoire: twelve new R2 entries (sent to the collector, not listed here), and two transcription slips of ours exposed and corrected.

Cheap structure tests on the new pages (overlap, frequency order, rank-for-rank decode). Corrections found: an earlier overlap figure (87-95% 'same code') was wrong because the old pool mixes codes; 701119 is Favre-family, not a fourth family; 701023 block 2 is R1; a seven-group run first read on 2emeS-2 does not exist on the scan.

Publication: the collector agreed (relayed by the project owner) that his scans and the transcriptions of them are published on the site and in the repository. Published: his transcription files and the derived sequence and alignment outputs in the target folder, the AI transcriptions of the twelve page scans (workbook with reliability notes, per-page text zip) under docs/data/pigeongrammes1870/, and six cropped snips of the scans on the page. Not published (outside the permission): repertoires R1-R3, his Excel files, the R2 gap table (a count only), the zip. Re-ran alpha_test, spell_solver, apply_telegram and joint_loop on the published files and they reproduce the committed outputs; bench_loop needs his Repertoire1.xlsx.

outcome.method_basis: The table is an alphabetical lexicon over 0000-9999 and words spelled between beacon groups decode, but only 20 hand-assigned entries are supported (12.5% of 608 coded non-beacon group occurrences); no sentence of the coded text reads and the engine accepted nothing safely.
outcome.fraction_read_source: wiki/index.md and wiki/syntheses/Z01.md: share of the 608 coded (non-beacon) group occurrences with an accepted reading, 20 supported entries all assigned by hand; the 128 beacon groups are not counted
outcome.notes: Not read. Structure found: alphabetical lexicon, spelled names (Steenackers, Mercadier, pigeons, Trochu) and a last paragraph of family news. Needs a second text in the inspectors' code or a printed copy of the circular; no such text is in the collection. Pillon's scans and the transcriptions of them are published with his permission (8 Nov 2026; DATA_NOT_INCLUDED.md); his repertoires R1-R3 and Excel files are not. The work on the Favre / delegation code (Chaudordy letter, 18 Dec 1870) is a different cipher, still in progress, with no page of its own yet. Second round (8 Nov 2026): 12 further page scans transcribed for the collector; three codes identified in them (R1, R2, the Favre/delegation code); the 13 Nov Tours telegram decodes with the collector's R2 and matches its printed text. The inspectors' code itself has no second text, so this target's outcome is unchanged.

credits.note: owns the collection and the scan of the telegram, sent the files and his transcription, confirmed that the clear words are in the original; suggested the beacon groups (0101, 0201, 0301) as brackets and that the table is almost alphabetical; offered readings that were tested (5926, 0603, 2215 failed; a Mercadier decomposition was withdrawn by him)

his hand transcription of the 2 November telegram and the group lists of the Chaudordy letter; the page scans (twelve of them were transcribed from images by Claude and checked against his hand transcription on a pilot); agreed on 8 Nov 2026 that his scans and the transcriptions are published
